1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 31.08.2024.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 31.08.2024 at about 7-45 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Sathanoor Police Station, on Halaguru - Kanakapura National Highway, near Sathanur Indian Oil Petrol Bunk when the Petitioner was walking on the left side of the road near said petrol bunk, at that time the accused/rider of the offending Passion Plus Motor Cycle bearing M.V.C.No.7170/2024 3 SCCH - 7 registration No.KA-10-EF-9739 drove the same from Sathanuru towards Kanakapura side in high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against him from back side
, as a result he sustained grievous injuries to right hand, left neck bone, back bone and left side chest.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Sathanoor Government Hospital and for higher treatment he was shifted to CDSIMER Hospital, Haronalli wherein he was treated as inpatient and undergone surgery therein and he has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical e x p e n d i t u r e a n d o t h e r i n c i d e n t a l c h a r g e s .
I n t h i s r e g a r d t h e w i f e o f t h e Petitioner/informant/Alamelamma has lodged complaint before the Sathanoor police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.116/2024 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 281, 125(a) and 125(b) of BNS and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
3.

Further it is contended that, prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and he was aged about 52 years and he was working as Security Guard at India Agro Farm house,
Doddabadagere and M.V.C.No.7170/2024 4 SCCH - 7 earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.

Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he lost his income and future prospective life, happiness,
and earning capacity and become disabled and dependent.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the rider of the offending Passion Plus Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-10-EF-9739.
Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.

sentences.text: The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Complaint, Ex.P3/spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4/Vehicle seizer mahazar, Ex.P-5/MVA report, Ex.P-6/Wound Certificate and Ex.P.7/Charge Sheet clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.

It is not in dispute as to the aspect that,
the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the M.V.C.No.7170/2024 16 SCCH - 7 accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P6/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281, 125(a) and 125(b) of BNS.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
21. Issue No.2:-

The Learned counsel for the Petitioner has contended that the injured Petitioner was aged about 52 years and he was working as Security Guard at India Agro farm house,
Doddabadagere and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., and the Petitioner has incurred heavy expenses towards medical expenditure.

As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of M.V.C.No.7170/2024 17 SCCH - 7 pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses, special diet,
conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

22. On the other hand, the learned counsel for Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that his earning was about Rs.30,000/- p.m., the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.
Since the Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.

23. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 52 years and he relied on the Ex.P.10/Adhar Card of the Petitioner, wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 01.03.1969 and this accident was took place on 31.08.2024.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 55 years 5 months.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 55 years.

24. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and M.V.C.No.7170/2024 18 SCCH - 7 negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was working as Security Guard at India Agro farm house, Doddabadagere and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.,.
But he has not produced single piece of document to prove his actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Tagur Shashishekar S V vs Ragini on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42683909/
7 Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2024, the notional income of the Petitioner is taken at Rs.15,750/-.

sentences.text: In the chief examination of PW-3/Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon deposed that in the alleged road traffic accident the petitioner has sustained open type I fracture of the dorsal barton right radius fracture with closed medial 1/3rd left clavicle fracture and fracture of the transverse process of L3 and L4 vertebra and the Petitioner was treated at CDSIMER Hospital with ORIF with plate and screws for the right distal radius on 03.09.2024 and later discharged on 16.09.2024.

Further deposed that now the Petitioner complains of pain and weakness in the right wrist, unable to lift weights, in the right hand and carry his routine work as before and on examination the Petitioner has restricted M.V.C.No.7170/2024 19 SCCH - 7 right wrist movements, wasting of the right forearm muscles and recent X-ray of the right wrist shows united fracture with implants in situ.

Further deposed that the Petitioner has sustained total disability of the right arm at 38% and whole body disability at 13% and the Petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of implant and the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
In support of his oral evidence, the doctor/PW-2 has produced Ex.P-13/Clinical notes and Ex.P-14/X-rays.

In the cross-examination of PW-2 by the counsel for Respondent No.2 he has deposed he has not treated doctor of the Petitioner and he has gone through Discharge Summary, Wound Certificate, X-ray Films and Case Sheet and follow-up treatment records and he has examined the Petitioner and assessed his disability.
The Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his right hand and left shoulder clavicle fracture.
The Petitioner has undergone surgery for right hand elbow and simple surgery on his left shoulder clavicle.
He has not taken advice from the treated doctor and now the fracture is united and the Petitioner is taking followup treatment.
In the follow-up records the doctor advised him to take physiotherapy treatment.
Further he has denied that as the fracture is united the Petitioner is M.V.C.No.7170/2024 20 SCCH - 7 hale and healthy.
Further he has denied that the Petitioner is not having any disability and he is hale and healthy and he is not suffering any pain or difficulties.
Further he denied that in order to help the petitioner he has assessed disability on the higher side and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.

26. As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as working as Security Guard and while doing his work the petitioner has to stand and sit for long time, he has to bend, put weight on both legs and hands, he has to sit down and difficulties in movements of elbow, forearm and wrist while doing the work.
But due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident the petitioner has not in position to do work as past.
The doctor has assessed the total disability of the right arm at 38% and whole body disability at 13%.
Hence by considering the age, occupation, nature of injury and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 13% to the whole body.
27. With regard to the quantum, the age of the petitioner is considered as 55 years and the income is considered at Rs.15,750/- p.m.
As per Sarala Varma's Case the multiplier 11 is applicable and functional disability is considered at 13%.
On considering the avocation and M.V.C.No.7170/2024 21 SCCH - 7 age of the petitioner, the total loss of future income is calculated as (Rs.15,750/- X 12 X 11 X 13/100) = Rs.2,70,270/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs.2,70,270/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.

In the alleged accident the petitioner has sustained sustained open type I fracture of the dorsal barton right radius fracture with closed medial 1/3rd left clavicle fracture and fracture of the transverse process of L3 and L4 vertebra and the Petitioner was treated at CDSIMER Hospital with ORIF with plate and screws for the right distal radius on 03.09.2024 and later discharged on 16.09.2024, which shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering,

29. Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at CDSIMER Hospital for a period from 01.09.2024 to 16.09.2024, i.e., for a period of 16 days.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.80,000/- (Rs.5,000/- per day X 16 days) under head of special diet and conveyance.
. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
31. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.94,500/- (Rs.15,750/- x 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
32. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical expenses as per Ex.P.9 for an amount of Rs.7,074/-.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,074/- under the head of hospital and medical expenses.
33. In the evidence affidavit of PW-2/doctor has stated that the Petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which would cost about Rs.60,000/-.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.60,000/-
compensation under the head future medical expenses.

In the result I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.7,11,844/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Eleven Thousand Eight Hundred and Forty Four only) with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Amount awarded under the future medical expenses does not carry future interest.
Further, Respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 31.08.2024.
, as a result he sustained grievous injuries to right hand, left neck bone, back bone and left side chest.
Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.116/2024 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 281, 125(a) and 125(b) of BNS and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
3.
Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he lost his income and future prospective life, happiness,
and earning capacity and become disabled and dependent.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the rider of the offending Passion Plus Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-10-EF-9739.
negligence attributed against the driver/accused of the offending vehicle and contended that the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance company and any liability, i.e.,

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V. Act., and violated M.V.C.No.7170/2024 6 SCCH - 7 terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
opennyai_summary.issue:
:: I S S U E S ::
(1) Whether the Petitioner proves that on 31-08-2024 at about 7-45 p.m, when he was pedestrian on extreme side of Sathnoor - Kanakapura road near Petrol Bunk,
NH-948 road,Sathanoor Village and Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District at that time,
the driver of offending Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-10-EF-9739 drove the same at high speed in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against him from his behind.
As a result of forced impact, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries?
(2) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
(3) What order or award?
As per final order,
 for the following.......
:REASONS:
11. Issue No.1:- This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act  1989 for seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the alleged accident.
12.

13.

The Respondent No.2 contended that the accused is innocent and falsely implicated by the police and the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the Petitioner M.V.C.No.7170/2024 12 SCCH - 7 and the said pedestrian Petitioner crossed the road on taking note of the approaching offending vehicle and the rider of the offending vehicle cannot save accident, however, slowly he may be riding and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent and in order to prove its version the Respondent No.2 has neither stepped into the witness box nor produced documents and any how the Respondent No.2 cross-examined the PW-1.
The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed the said Accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle, the said pedestrian Petitioner crossed the road on taking note of the approaching offending vehicle and the rider of the offending vehicle cannot save accident, however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent and the alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 55 years 5 months.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 55 years.
But he has not produced single piece of document to prove his actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.
Hence, in order to prove his case,
the Petitioner himself examined as P.W.1 and he has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.12 documents.
On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, mahazar,
Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash M.V.C.No.7170/2024 15 SCCH - 7 and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the Tagur Shashishekar S V vs Ragini on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42683909/
6 same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P6/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281, 125(a) and 125(b) of BNS.
opennyai_summary.decision:
On considering the avocation and M.V.C.No.7170/2024 21 SCCH - 7 age of the petitioner, the total loss of future income is calculated as (Rs.15,750/- X 12 X 11 X 13/100) = Rs.2,70,270/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs.2,70,270/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.80,000/- (Rs.5,000/- per day X 16 days) under head of special diet and conveyance.
. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
31. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.94,500/- (Rs.15,750/- x 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
32. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical expenses as per Ex.P.9 for an amount of Rs.7,074/-.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,074/- under the head of hospital and medical expenses.
33. In the evidence affidavit of PW-2/doctor has stated that the Petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which would cost about Rs.60,000/-.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.60,000/-
compensation under the head future medical expenses.
34.
The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:
M.V.C.No.7170/2024 23 SCCH - 7 Sl. Compensation under different heads Amount in No. (Rs) 1 Loss of future income due to disability 2,70,270-00 2 Pain and suffering, mental agony 1,00,000-00 3
Special diet and conveyance 80,000-00 4 Loss of amenities 1,00,000-00 5 Loss of income during laid up period 94,500-00 6
Actual medical expenses 7,074-00 7
Future medical expenses 60,000-00 Total 7,11,844-00 35.
The Petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,11,844/-.
36.
Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent Tagur Shashishekar S V vs Ragini on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42683909/
9 No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Issue No.3:
In the result I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.7,11,844/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Eleven Thousand Eight Hundred and Forty Four only) with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Amount awarded under the future medical expenses does not carry future interest.
Further, Respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
